globalLanguage.background: Continuous BackgroundField across the entire timeline: drifting radial well + faint gold linear wash + vignette. Never resets between scenes — that is what stops the cuts feeling like PowerPoint transitions.
globalLanguage.transitionStyle: Cross-dissolve with a slow Ken Burns push (1.015 → 1.045 over the scene). Implemented in SceneFrame; every scene wraps in it.
globalLanguage.easing: ease-out cubic on opacity; near-linear on scale.

audio.policy: Played once across the whole video. Never split, never re-encoded, never per-scene.

globalLanguage.parallax: BackgroundField sin/cos drift (period = full timeline) provides subtle parallax. Foreground scenes do not parallax independently — that would compete with the type.

rules: Opening + closing scenes: TenTrinity Carbon horizontal-white at hero scale, centred. (Opening is currently NOT a logo scene — first scene is a statement; logo lands on closing only.)
Section dividers: icon-gold may be used very small if a divider scene is added. Currently no section dividers are scheduled.
Content scenes (clips 1–12): no logo. The brand carries through type, palette, and motion language.
Treatment: opacity fade-in only; never spin, bounce, glow, or scale-pop.

perScene.scene-13: horizontal-white at hero, fade-in over 27 frames, max opacity 0.95

typography.display: Inter / SF Pro Display / Helvetica Neue / system-ui
rules: Anything below 24px reads as a slide deck, not a film — never use it for visible content.
Tabular numerals on every numeric figure (fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums').
Letter-spacing is negative on display-weight type (-1 to -3) and positive on mono kickers (+4 to +8).

pacing.policy: Scenes follow the 13 AAF Clip boundaries. Sentence-level cues drive in-scene reveal beats only — they never cause hard cuts.
rules: Title beat lands within the first 0.6s of each scene; everything else slots in around the cues.
Final beat of each scene resolves at least 0.6s before scene end so the cross-dissolve has room.
Hero metric (scene-11) holds ≥1.5s after count-up resolves.
Closing scene holds ≥7s on the three lines before the synchronous audio + visual fade.

transitions.global: SceneFrame cross-dissolve + slow Ken Burns. Default.
transitions.perScene: All scenes use the global transition. There are no wipes, slides, peels, page-flips, or zoom-bursts. Anywhere.
transitions.outroFade: Final 1.2–1.4s of scene-13 fades the visual; the master audio bed fades by the same envelope.

metricsAnimation.countUp: Ease-out cubic from 0 to target. Duration ~1.6s. Values formatted with tabular numerals; prefix/suffix preserved (so '−16.3', '700K+', '$1.2B' stay intact).
metricsAnimation.delay: Tied to the cue when the narrator says the figure. Default offset: 0.2s after scene start, then per-cue.
metricsAnimation.settle: Final value holds with no further motion until the next beat or scene end.

chartsAnimation.policy: No bar charts in this cut. Numerical comparisons are handled by MetricsScene (clip 4) and the hero MetricScene (clip 11). If a chart is added later, the rule is: bars and figures finish at the same frame — never staggered final values.

beats.action: title fades up; word stagger; gold rule travels left-to-right

scenes.cinematicNotes: Editorial open. Resist any motion below the type — the scene should read as a film opening, not as a slide.

beats.action: creed line 1 lands; gold rule travels in beside it

scenes.cinematicNotes: Three creed lines. The narration lays them out in sequence — the visual matches that sequence beat-for-beat.
Pillar reveals are timed to 'The first / second / third is…' cues. Resist crowding the second pillar against the first — the takaful row needs its own beat.

beats.action: metric 04 (Lloyd's) lands as text, not number

scenes.cinematicNotes: Each figure resolves on the cue word. Tabular numerals; never two figures animating at once.
Left column is a deliberate slow read — the muted column is the 'before'. The right column lands on the cue 'TenTrinity Carbon takes a different approach' and inherits the gold accent.

Longest scene of the film (81.0s). Pace is the point — the four constructs need air. Use Arabic transliteration as the kicker for the first three rows; 'Lloyd's' anchors the last row in the operational world.
Five protections is the ceiling. Each row tight — kicker / label / one body line. Cues fall roughly every 7–8s in the middle of clip 7.
Row 03 (governance) carries the most words — keep its sub-line tight: 'Shariah oversight aligned with AAOIFI and IFSB.' Don't add the carbon-market frameworks line on screen; the narration covers it.

beats.action: tail line ('not a separate cryptocurrency exposure')

scenes.cinematicNotes: Both columns gold-accented. The narration's pivot at ~33s is the cue for the right column. The tail line is essential — it draws the boundary with crypto.

beats.action: Gabon (right) region reveals; gold rule travels in vertically

scenes.cinematicNotes: No literal map. Restraint reads as confidence at this register. Coordinates in mono caption are sufficient.

beats.action: eyebrow fades in; gold rule travels

scenes.cinematicNotes: The single most important visual moment. Number is the picture. Hold the final value for at least 1.5s before any other motion. Negative sign uses the proper Unicode minus (−).
Brisker pacing — the narration is dense. Reveals every ~5s; the closing line gets the rest of the scene's tail.

beats.action: horizontal-white logo fades in at hero scale
gold rule scales horizontally beneath logo

scenes.cinematicNotes: Longest hold of the film, in real terms relative to its 26.9s span. The logo is the only graphic element. Ends with simultaneous audio and visual fade — the master voiceover never gets a hard cut.

avoid: Spinning, bouncing, elastic springs, or any toy motion.
Clipart, stickers, emoji, generic SaaS template visuals.
More than 6 bullets on screen at once.
Tiny copy. Anything below 24px reads as a slide deck.
Showing the original PowerPoint screenshot as the main video.
Per-scene wipes / slides / peels / dissolves other than the global cross-dissolve.
Watermarking the logo on every frame.
